_note: Indonesian has no person or tense conjugation, so the Gym drills the affix system instead — that IS the productive morphology. The meN-/peN- nasal alternation and the -kan/-i pair are the two things a learner has to automate before reading is possible.

entries.point: The meN- prefix: active transitive verbs
entries.label: meN- active
entries.usage: Nasal adapts to the root; p/t/k/s drop.
entries.example: baca → membaca

entries.point: The ber- prefix: intransitive and stative verbs
entries.label: ber- intransitive
entries.usage: No object. be- before r.
entries.example: renang → berenang

entries.point: The di- passive: putting the object first
entries.label: di- passive
entries.usage: Everyday word order, not formal.
entries.example: Buku itu dibaca.

entries.label: -kan
entries.usage: Cause it, or do it for someone.
entries.example: beli → membelikan

entries.label: -i
entries.usage: Object is a place or surface.
entries.example: duduk → menduduki

entries.point: The ter- prefix: accidental, stative, capable
entries.label: ter-
entries.usage: Accidental, resulting state, or capable.
entries.example: jatuh → terjatuh

entries.label: memper-
entries.usage: Make something more X.
entries.example: besar → memperbesar

entries.label: Passive 1 vs 2
entries.usage: di- for third person; bare root for 1st/2nd.
entries.example: Buku itu saya baca.

entries.label: No conjugation
entries.usage: The verb never changes, whoever is doing it and whenever it happens.
entries.example: Saya mau makan. — I want to eat.

entries.label: tidak vs bukan
entries.usage: tidak denies an action or a quality; bukan denies a thing.
entries.example: Rumah ini tidak besar. — This house isn't big.

entries.point: Time markers before the verb: sudah, belum, akan
entries.label: sudah / belum / akan
entries.usage: One word in front of the verb: done, not yet, still to come.
entries.example: Saya sudah makan. — I have already eaten.

entries.point: Aspect markers: sedang, masih, pernah, baru
entries.label: sedang / masih / pernah
entries.usage: Going on now, still true, ever done, or only just done.
entries.example: Saya sedang makan sekarang. — I'm eating right now.

entries.label: bisa / boleh / harus
entries.usage: Can, may, must, want — straight before the verb, never changed.
entries.example: Saya bisa berbicara bahasa Indonesia. — I can speak Indonesian.

entries.label: ada
entries.usage: There is, is present, and casually to have; tidak ada for none.
entries.example: Ada masalah dengan komputer ini. — There is a problem with this computer.

entries.label: No doer, or oleh
entries.usage: The usual passive names nobody; oleh adds the doer.
entries.example: Rumah itu dijual tahun lalu. — That house was sold last year.

entries.label: Affix pairs
entries.usage: Pick by who or what the object is: mengajar a subject, mengajari a person, mengajarkan a topic to someone.
entries.example: Dia mengajar matematika di sekolah. — She teaches mathematics at the school.

entries.label: Frozen affixes
entries.usage: Words that look built from a root but are learned whole.
entries.example: Saya tidak mengerti maksud Anda. — I don't understand what you mean.

entries.point: Register: baku, colloquial, and Jakarta speech
entries.label: Colloquial speech
entries.usage: How people actually talk: gue, lu, nggak, and -in for -kan.
entries.example: Gue nggak tahu. — I don't know.

entries.label: Register switching
entries.usage: News and novels narrate formally and let people speak casually.
entries.example: Menteri menyatakan bahwa harga akan stabil. — The minister stated that prices would be stable.

entries.label: News style
entries.usage: Reporting leads with the thing affected and leaves out the rest.
entries.example: Tersangka ditangkap polisi tadi malam. — The suspect was arrested by police last night.

entries.label: peN- agent
entries.usage: Same nasal rule as meN-.
entries.example: tulis → penulis

entries.label: ke-an / per-an
entries.usage: Abstractions and processes.
entries.example: bebas → kebebasan

entries.point: The se- prefix: one, same, whole
entries.label: se-
entries.usage: One, same-as, as…as, the whole of.
entries.example: besar → sebesar

entries.label: Comparison
entries.usage: lebih … daripada; paling / ter-.
entries.example: lebih tinggi daripada

entries.label: Classifiers
entries.usage: orang people, ekor animals, buah things.
entries.example: tiga orang guru

entries.label: Reduplication
entries.usage: Casual, various, reciprocal — not only plural.
entries.example: jalan-jalan

entries.label: Adjective order
entries.usage: The describing word comes after the thing it describes.
entries.example: Dia tinggal di rumah besar. — He lives in a big house.

entries.label: Possession
entries.usage: Name the thing, then the owner — no extra word between them.
entries.example: Ini rumah saya. — This is my house.

entries.label: Plural: buku-buku
entries.usage: Say the word twice when you mean more than one of it.
entries.example: Di rumah ada buku-buku. — There are books at home.

entries.label: apakah questions
entries.usage: Put apakah at the front; nothing else in the sentence moves.
entries.example: Apakah kamu mau makan? — Do you want to eat?

entries.point: Formal vs. informal "you"; inclusive vs. exclusive "we"
entries.label: Pronoun choice
entries.usage: kamu is casual, Anda polite; kita includes the listener, kami doesn't.
entries.example: Anda mau makan? — Would you like to eat? (formal/polite)

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: apa, siapa, di mana, kapan — each sits where the answer would.
entries.example: Kamu tinggal di mana? — Where do you live?

entries.label: di / ke / dari
entries.usage: At or in, to, and from — put one before the place.
entries.example: Buku itu ada di atas meja. — The book is on the table.

entries.label: yang
entries.usage: Hangs a whole description on a noun: the one that…
entries.example: Orang yang tinggi itu guru saya. — That tall person is my teacher.

entries.label: untuk / supaya
entries.usage: Say what something is for, or why you are doing it.
entries.example: Saya datang untuk belajar. — I came to study.

entries.label: kalau / jika
entries.usage: If this, then that — kalau when speaking, jika when writing.
entries.example: Kalau hujan, saya tidak pergi. — If it rains, I won't go.

entries.label: bahwa
entries.usage: Passing on what someone said or thought, with no change of tense.
entries.example: Dia mengatakan bahwa dia akan datang. — He said that he would come.

entries.label: -lah / -kah / -pun
entries.usage: Tiny endings that soften, ask, or point at the important word.
entries.example: Dialah yang bertanggung jawab. — HE is the one responsible.

entries.label: Written connectors
entries.usage: The joining words written Indonesian runs on: sehingga, meskipun, namun.
entries.example: Hujan deras, sehingga jalan banjir. — It rained hard, so the road flooded.

entries.label: Formal noun style
entries.usage: Formal writing turns actions into things: pembangunan, penelitian.
entries.example: Pembangunan jalan tol sedang berlangsung. — Construction of the toll road is underway.
